interface.name: picowl_buffer_manager_v1
interface.description: Lets a client obtain a buffer allocated by the compositor (a dmabuf fd). The client wraps the fd into a wl_buffer with zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1 (create_params, params.add with the fd, stride, offset and modifier from the dmabuf event, then params.create_immed with the same size and format). The compositor advertises whether an output copies damage to device memory. Clients then start with one buffer and may draw into it again after a copied event; when a retained event answers a commit instead, they switch to a second buffer and use wl_buffer.release.

request.name: create_buffer
request.description: Only DRM_FORMAT_RGB565 (0x36314752) is accepted. The result is reported with dmabuf and done, or failed.

event.name: format
event.description: Sent once per supported format when the manager is bound.

event.name: copy_type
event.description: Sent on bind and whenever it changes. 1 means an output copies damage to device memory: copied events may follow direct-scanout commits and the client may redraw into the same buffer after one. 0 means scanout: copied is never sent, keep double buffering and use wl_buffer.release.

interface.name: picowl_buffer_v1
interface.description: Describes a dmabuf allocated by the compositor. Wrap the fd with zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1 (params.add + create_immed).

request.name: attach_surface
request.description: Commits of that surface are numbered from 1, with uint32 wrap (0 is skipped).

event.name: copied

description.summary: commits up to serial were copied out

event.description:
Only sent when copy_type is 1 and the output that showed the commit copied it straight from this buffer (direct scanout on a copy-type driver): all surface commits up to and including serial have been copied to device memory, and the buffer may be drawn into again without waiting for wl_buffer.release.
The compositor takes no snapshot. If the surface later has to be composited (a software cursor, popup or overlay appears over it, or the output is redrawn) before the client's next commit, the compositor re-reads the last committed buffer for the affected region. The client's next commit replaces that content; clients should therefore commit the complete frame, not partial updates.
Exactly one of copied and retained answers a commit, unless a newer commit supersedes it first.

event.name: retained

description.summary: the compositor keeps reading the buffer

event.description: The commit with this serial was not (or will not be) consumed by a copy-type direct scanout: it is composited, occluded, off-output, on a scanout-type output, or the output is disabled or blanked. The compositor keeps the buffer as the surface's current content and may read it at any time until a newer commit replaces it. The client must not draw into it, and has to use a second buffer for its next frame (allocated on demand) and wait for wl_buffer.release on this one, as with any buffer. Never sent for commits answered by copied. Sent also on outputs which are not copy-type, regardless of the copy_type value announced by the manager.
